checked.claim: On a GM's own client the Infiltrate rows (Dash, Echoes, Shut, Force, Pick, Keep Watch, Tail, Listen's eavesdrop) read the handler's raw `{ reply: {...} }` as if it were the reply, so the GM's card says the wrong result; a `{ refused }` is read as success by Dash and Echoes and is silent in the rest.
checked.why: Read the whole road. `ask` (bridge-table.mjs:1653-1661) spreads `opts` into bridgeRequest unchanged; createWaiter's local branch settles `{ ok: true, value }` with whatever `local` returned (bridge-guards.mjs:1947-1948), while a player's road is answered with `out?.reply` by the judge (1819) and read as `packet.value` (2030). The eight `local` closures of bridge-asks.mjs:65-150 return the handler's answer as is, and the handlers answer `{ reply: {...} }` (bridge-runs-acts.mjs:188, 204, 217 and the rest). The other `local` closures in the same file do unwrap - `return out?.reply ?? null` with `sayNotDone` on a refusal (bridge-asks.mjs:261-265, 293-297 and nine more) - which is the shape these eight lack. The readers check `res.value?.refused` (action-doors.mjs:41, 91, 152; action-watch.mjs:46; action-tail.mjs:94), so the refusal half of the raw shape was foreseen, but they then read `res.value?.forced`, `?.kept`, `?.seen`, `?.moves`, `?.room`, `?.moved` off the top, not off `.reply`. Dash (action-listen.mjs:354-356) and Echoes (322-325) do not test `refused`, so a refusal there reads as 0 crossings / nobody with the action kept spent. Nothing keeps a GM from these rows: performAction refuses only a player's `free` and a player with no GM (action-rolls.mjs:101, 117). No test presses a row on a GM's client: 33-bridge-paths runs performDash, performEchoes and performShut on p1 (1947, 2018, 2083); tier 0's entries only read the noGm literals (tests-tier0.mjs:10578-10584). Severity minor holds: the world state is right (the handler ran), only the GM's own card is wrong, and only when a GM plays a student.
